newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hails Tajik peace accord.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hails Tajik peace accord.

text.p: The United States called on Tajik factions to craft a lasting peace out of a sweeping deal signed Friday to end four years of civil war in the former Soviet republic.

"We urge the negotiating sides, and the whole Tajik nation, to take full advantage of this opportunity to move beyond its civil conflict, as it is only the Tajik sides themselves that can fulfil implementation of the accords," the State Department said.

In a statement, it said the deal represented a historic opportunity for Tajikistan to enter into a new political era, "one of building lasting national reconciliation, stability and economic development."
The conflict killed tens of thousands of people and forced many more from their homes in the Central Asian state of 5.7 million before a ceasefire was agreed last December.
The final accord -- brokered by Iran, Russia and the United Nations -- was endangered by last-minute wrangling over a stalled prisoner exchange and haggling over political power-sharing.
